title: Organ‐specific ozone and nitrogen legacies strengthen substrate control over litter decomposition
content:

Abstract

Elevated tropospheric ozone (O3) and nitrogen (N) deposition are concurrent atmospheric changes that strongly influence terrestrial carbon cycling, yet their combined effects on below-ground decomposition remain poorly understood. Using a free-air O3 concentration enrichment system (O3-FACE), we investigated how O3–N interactions influence the decomposition of poplar leaf and fine root litter by separating growth stage changes in litter chemistry from environmental effects in the decomposition stage. Decomposition responses were strongly organ-specific. Elevated O3 and N addition had only minor effects on leaf litter decay, whereas fine root decomposition was markedly suppressed, indicating a synergistic inhibition of below-ground carbon turnover. Lower quality substrates decomposed more slowly, released fewer nutrients (with phosphorus release reduced by up to 52.9%) and retained more mass (up to 10.6%), highlighting impaired nutrient recycling under concurrent atmospheric changes. Random forest modelling and path analyses identified starch concentration (leaves) and lignin/N ratios (fine roots) as the dominant controls on decomposition. Microbial community shifts influenced fine-root decay but played a smaller role than substrate chemical traits. Substrate legacies formed during plant growth exerted stronger control over the dynamics of decomposition than the decomposition environment. Collectively, our results demonstrate that atmospheric O3 and N inputs reprogram decomposition trajectories primarily through changes in substrate chemical quality, resulting in a decoupling between substrate chemistry and microbial regulation that constrains nutrient cycling and soil carbon stabilization. These findings provide mechanistic insight into how concurrent global atmospheric drivers regulate below-ground processes and shape soil carbon feedbacks under global change.

Abstract

近地面臭氧 (O3) 升高与氮 (N) 沉降是当前陆地生态系统面临的两类重要大气环境变化，并可能共同影响土壤碳循环过程。然而，二者如何通过改变植物凋落物质量及其分解环境，进而调控地上与地下凋落物分解，仍缺乏清晰认识。本研究依托自由空气臭氧浓度升高系统 (O3-FACE)，以杨树叶片和细根凋落物为对象，区分植物生长阶段形成的底物化学遗留效应与分解阶段环境效应，探讨 O3 与 N 交互作用对凋落物分解及养分释放的影响机制。 结果表明，凋落物分解对 O3 和 N 添加的响应具有明显的器官差异。叶片凋落物分解受处理影响相对较弱，而细根分解受到显著抑制，说明 O3 升高与 N 输入可能协同减缓地下碳周转。低质量底物通常表现出较慢的分解速率、较低的养分释放量和较高的质量残留，其中磷释放量最高降低 52.9%，质量残留最高增加 10.6%，表明复合大气变化可能削弱凋落物分解过程中的养分再循环。 随机森林模型和路径分析进一步表明，叶片凋落物分解主要受淀粉浓度调控，而细根分解主要受木质素/N 比驱动。微生物群落变化虽然参与调节细根分解过程，但其解释作用弱于底物化学性状。总体来看，植物生长阶段形成的底物遗留效应比分解阶段环境本身对分解动态具有更强的控制作用。 综上，本研究表明，O3 升高和 N 输入主要通过重塑凋落物底物化学质量改变分解轨迹，并可能削弱底物化学性状与微生物调控之间的耦合关系，从而影响养分循环和土壤碳稳定化过程。这些结果为理解多重全球变化因子如何调控地下分解过程及其土壤碳反馈提供了机制性证据。
